main_text.l: affectu precari, quos non sua malitia, sed
honestus error in piam hanc ( ut puta-
bant ) Rebellionem prodiderat.
Quâ enim eram in Illos charitate,
credebam, eorum plerosque non in Me,
sed in meos ( ut putabant) errores pugnâs-
se, nec eo animo ut perderent, sed ut
emendarent. Spero, Dei misericordiam
veniam huic errori dedisse, & eo usque
bonum animum eorum acceptâsse si-
mul & exaudivisse, ut, quemadmodum
me hactenus conservavit, ita per hæc
adversa præparaverit, ut illi melius in
posterum serviam, & fiam populi mei com-
modis, quàm superius fueram, atten-
tior.
Nec libentius ignosco in errorem se-
ductis, qui sic Fidem suam præposterè
per injurias declarant, quàm verè ex-
peto & enitar in posterum, omni bene
merendi occasione arrepta, injustas Su-
spiciones eximere, & quæ bene cogitârint,
remunerare.
Nimis enim sum affectus mei in po-
pulum conscius, ut in Illorum de Me,
mutuò, suspicionem adducar, nec ulla
hostium malitia eo me solatio fraudabit,
quod ex hac fiducia percipio. Nunquam
ita indulgebo paucorum livori, ut, quod

page.notes: The symbol before "Nec libentius" at the start of that paragraph is a printed paragraph mark that I could not read with certainty; I have left it out. The word "Suspiciones" is split by the printed hyphen at the line end as "Su-spiciones" and is italic. The catchword "fraudes" is set at the lower right and is not repeated in the text. Accents on "Quâ", "pugnâsse", "acceptâsse" and "quàm" are as printed. The spelling "præparaverit" is as printed on the scan.
